clue.text: Doctor man's cut in private room

definitions.note: a singular noun phrase, matching the answer

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A doctor gets a haircut in a private consulting room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' looks like a person; it is a verb telling you to rearrange MANSCUT.
explanation.definitionFit: A sanctum is a secluded inner room where someone can be undisturbed, a study or den.

clue.text: Small happy dog's air of superiority

parts.note: a happy dog wags its tail, so it is a wagger

explanation.surface: A little cheerful dog has a superior air about it.
explanation.definitionFit: Swagger is a confident, arrogant manner or bearing that suggests self-importance.

clue.text: One of those sweet words of affection or love

definitions.text: One of those sweet words of affection
definitions.meaning: sweet ... are tender words whispered between lovers
in tennis scoring love means zero

explanation.surface: A tender word of fondness, or of love.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweet nothings are words of endearment, and a zero score in tennis is love.

clue.text: Charge for bridge, going over river to do some fishing

indicators.note: going over means covering on both sides, so the charge surrounds the river letter

parts.note: a toll is a fee paid to cross a bridge or road

explanation.surface: Paying to cross a bridge over a river to go fishing.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface bridge also hints at the fairy-tale creature living under one.
explanation.definitionFit: To troll is to fish by trailing a baited line behind a moving boat.

clue.text: Sources of information for many as dim as me, possibly

indicators.note: possibly means the letters may be arranged differently

explanation.surface: Where people as dim as the speaker get their news.
explanation.definitionFit: Newspapers, television and radio reach large audiences and are where most people get their news.

clue.text: Like debonair young man in a hurry

definitions.meaning: stylish and attractive, as a dapper young man is

explanation.surface: A dapper young man is rushing somewhere.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both stylishly attractive and moving off quickly, two separate senses of one adjective.

clue.text: European money formerly put into education

indicators.note: put into means the letters sit inside the word education

explanation.surface: Old continental cash invested in schooling.
explanation.definitionFit: A ducat was a gold coin once used in many European countries, notably Venice.

clue.text: Hit it big, ultimately, in royal house in European city

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the picked letters go into the royal house

parts.note: the Stuarts were a royal house of Scotland and England

indicators.note: ultimately points to the last letter of each of the three words

explanation.surface: Someone makes it big while staying in a royal palace abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ultimately' takes T, T and G; 'in' puts them inside STUART.
explanation.definitionFit: Stuttgart is a major city in southwest Germany, capital of Baden-Württemberg.

clue.text: Understanding not absent from mind, proverbially

definitions.meaning: deep perception or grasp of something
the proverb 'out of sight, out of mind' implies that what is visible stays in the mind

explanation.surface: Insight means keeping things in mind, as the proverb says.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as IN SIGHT, the opposite of 'out of sight' in the proverb.
explanation.definitionFit: Insight is perceptive comprehension; read as two words, it means visible, so kept in mind.

clue.text: Sourcebook?

parts.note: the book telling of the origin of everything, the first in the Bible

explanation.definitionFit: Genesis, meaning origin, is the opening book of the Bible describing creation.

clue.text: Writes a short novel about university

indicators.note: about means going round, so the rearranged letters surround the university letter
novel means new or fresh, so the letters of a and short take a new order

explanation.surface: Someone pens a brief novel concerning a university.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like a noun but is the anagram signal: ASHORT becomes ATHORS, and 'about' puts it round U.
explanation.definitionFit: To author a work is to write it; both verbs are in the third person singular.

clue.text: Advises what's one essential to make a crossword popular

parts.words: what's one essential to make a crossword
parts.note: a crossword cannot exist without its clues, one of its essential ingredients
in means fashionable or popular, as in 'the in thing'

explanation.surface: Tips on how to make a crossword catch on.
explanation.walkthrough: The long middle phrase is a cryptic description standing for a single word.
explanation.definitionFit: To clue someone in is to inform or tip them off, giving them the facts they need.

clue.text: Bird taking most of fruit — shame about that

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for shame goes round the shortened fruit

parts.note: guilt is the feeling of shame at wrongdoing

indicators.note: most of means the final letter of the fruit is dropped

parts.note: a lemon is a citrus fruit

explanation.surface: A bird helps itself to nearly all of some fruit and feels bad about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shame' reads as the bird's feeling but supplies the outer letters; 'most of' trims the fruit and 'about' wraps the shame word round it.
explanation.definitionFit: The guillemot is a black-and-white seabird of the auk family that nests on cliffs.

clue.text: Old clothes in which to chatter idly

parts.note: to gas is informal for chattering away at length

explanation.surface: Antique garments in which one might sit and gossip.
explanation.definitionFit: Togas were the loose outer garments worn by citizens of ancient Rome.

clue.text: Appropriate port for ship? On the contrary

definitions.text: port for ship? On the contrary
definitions.meaning: port is a ship's left side, and the contrary of left is the opposite direction, starboard

explanation.surface: Asking which harbour suits a vessel, then reversing the question.
explanation.walkthrough: Port is the left-hand side of a ship; 'On the contrary' asks for the opposite side.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means suitable or correct, and it is also the side opposite left.

clue.text: Large number in middle of summer

definitions.meaning: the middle letters of summer are MM, the Roman numeral for two thousand

explanation.surface: Crowds at the height of the season.
explanation.walkthrough: 'summer' suggests the season; its centre letters MM are Roman for two thousand.
explanation.definitionFit: Thousands means a very great many, and MM is two thousand in Roman numerals.

clue.text: Philosopher, self-proclaimed existential thinker?

definitions.meaning: a French thinker of the seventeenth century
his famous dictum 'I think, therefore I am' declares that he exists because he thinks

explanation.surface: A philosopher who calls himself an existentialist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'existential' suggests Sartre-style existentialism, but it means proving one's own existence: 'Cogito, ergo sum'.
explanation.definitionFit: René Descartes was the French philosopher who founded modern rationalism with his cogito.

clue.text: Illicit tapes show awful working environment

indicators.note: illicit means improper, so the letters of tapes show are put in an improper order

explanation.surface: Secret recordings expose terrible factory conditions.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweatshop is a factory where workers endure long hours, low pay and poor conditions.

clue.text: Newspaper partly concealing crime in minister's house

indicators.note: concealing means holding inside, so the newspaper part wraps round the crime

parts.note: a page is one part of a newspaper
arson is the crime of setting fire to property

explanation.surface: A paper's report hints at wrongdoing at the vicar's home.
explanation.definitionFit: A parsonage is the residence provided for a parish priest or minister by the church.

clue.text: People's leader elevated and honoured

indicators.note: leader means the first letter of People's

parts.note: raised means lifted up or elevated

explanation.surface: A popular leader is promoted and given honours.
explanation.definitionFit: To praise someone is to commend them, so praised means lauded or honoured.

clue.text: Change order right before meal — dig in without starters

indicators.note: before puts the right letter ahead of the rest
without starters means the first letter of each of meal, dig and in is removed

explanation.surface: Someone changes their food order just before tucking in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without starters' drops M, D and I from meal, dig, in, leaving EAL, IG, N.
explanation.definitionFit: To realign something is to arrange it differently, putting it into a new order.

clue.text: The thankyou letter coming from Athens originally

parts.note: ta is informal British for thank you

explanation.surface: A thank-you note that was first sent from Athens.
explanation.definitionFit: Theta is the eighth character of the Greek alphabet, which originated in ancient Greece.

clue.text: Beethoven's work, including his fourth, is rousing stuff

indicators.note: including means taking in, so the symphony holds the extra letter

parts.note: the Eroica is Beethoven's Third Symphony
his refers to Beethoven, whose fourth letter is T

clue.text: Question one about name obliquely

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for one goes round the name letter

parts.note: an ace is a one in cards or dice

explanation.surface: Someone queries a single detail about a name.
explanation.definitionFit: To look askance is to glance sideways, with suspicion; the adverb means sidelong.

clue.text: Construction associated with Hoover when put in as US president

explanation.walkthrough: Hoover suggests the president, but here it names the Hoover Dam.
explanation.definitionFit: John Adams and his son John Quincy Adams were the second and sixth American presidents.

clue.text: Movie director set to shoot after brief hold-up

parts.note: a hitch is a temporary snag or delay

explanation.definitionFit: Alfred Hitchcock was the English film-maker famed for suspense thrillers such as Psycho.

clue.text: Badger member of undistinguished trio

definitions.meaning: to badger is to pester or harass

explanation.surface: A badger belongs to a dull threesome.

clue.text: Pour cold water on a book of prophecy

parts.note: to hose something is to spray water over it

explanation.walkthrough: 'Pour cold water on' suggests rejecting, but it is meant literally.

clue.text: Evil-doer holding power, professional propagandist?

parts.note: a sinner is one who does wrong

clue.text: Having reformed, in ashes and sackcloth

clue.text: A lot of rulers can be extremely dastardly and disagreeable

parts.note: nasty means unpleasant or disagreeable

clue.text: A pacifist finally in position to pacify

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of pacifist
